🌾 When to plant sorghum (guinea corn) in Nigeria

Also called Dawa (Hausa) and Ọkà bàbà (Yoruba).

Quick answer: Plant sorghum (guinea corn) in Nigeria from May to July and harvest from October to December. Planted with the northern rains (May–July) and harvested as the dry season begins (October–December).

PlantMay to July
HarvestOctober to December
Grows inNorth-West, North-East and North-Central
TypeGrains & cereals
Local namesDawa · Ọkà bàbà

About sorghum (guinea corn)

Nigeria is one of Africa's largest sorghum producers. It is used for tuwo, kunu, ogi and the malt drinks industry.

How to plant sorghum (guinea corn) well

Thresh and dry grain thoroughly. Store in airtight bags off the floor.

Planted with the northern rains (May–July) and harvested as the dry season begins (October–December).

Diseases and pests of sorghum (guinea corn)

  • Striga (witchweed, parasitic plant)Use Striga-tolerant varieties and rotate with legumes like cowpea or soybean.
  • Grain mouldChoose varieties that mature after the rains stop and harvest on time.

Best states for sorghum (guinea corn)

Kano · Katsina · Kaduna · Bauchi · Borno · Gombe · Niger · Jigawa · Zamfara · Adamawa

Questions farmers ask

When is the best time to plant sorghum (guinea corn) in Nigeria?

Plant sorghum (guinea corn) in Nigeria from May to July and harvest from October to December. Planted with the northern rains (May–July) and harvested as the dry season begins (October–December).

What is sorghum (guinea corn) called in Yoruba, Hausa and Igbo?

Sorghum (Guinea corn) is called Dawa (Hausa) and Ọkà bàbà (Yoruba).

When is sorghum (guinea corn) harvested in Nigeria?

Sorghum (Guinea corn) is usually harvested from October to December.

Which Nigerian states grow the most sorghum (guinea corn)?

Kano, Katsina, Kaduna, Bauchi, Borno, Gombe, Niger, Jigawa, Zamfara and Adamawa are among the best-known sorghum (guinea corn) states.

Can I grow sorghum (guinea corn) in my part of Nigeria?

Sorghum (Guinea corn) grows best in the North-West, North-East and North-Central regions. In other regions, ask your ADP extension officer before planting.

What diseases attack sorghum (guinea corn) and how do I prevent them?

Striga (witchweed, parasitic plant): Use Striga-tolerant varieties and rotate with legumes like cowpea or soybean. Grain mould: Choose varieties that mature after the rains stop and harvest on time.
